title: Knowledge Check 3 - Lessons 11-15
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 11-15 - Access to Records. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: An org wants reps to see only their own Opportunities and managers to see their team's. Which OWD is the correct foundation?
questions.explanation: Private OWD makes ownership (and hierarchy) the only path, so reps see their own and managers see subordinates via the hierarchy - exactly the baseline for 'my records plus my team'.

questions.question: Why does changing the OWD of a detail object in a master-detail relationship have no effect on record access?
options: The detail object is a standard object
Detail-child access is Controlled by Parent, so it inherits the master's sharing
questions.explanation: In master-detail, child access is fully inherited from the parent; the child's OWD setting is ignored (Controlled by Parent), so you configure the parent's sharing instead.

questions.question: A new custom object should be readable by everyone but editable only by owners. Which OWD should be set?
questions.explanation: Public Read Only grants universal read with owner-only edit. Private would hide records from non-owners, and Public Read/Write would let everyone edit.

questions.question: After adding a criteria-based sharing rule on Account, some records still don't share as expected. What is the most likely cause?
options: The rule was not recalculated after the underlying criteria data changed, or the records don't meet criteria
questions.explanation: Criteria rules evaluate against current field values and existing sharing rows; if the criteria data changed or the rule wasn't recalculated, the grants are stale. Sharing rules never remove access, and OWD Private doesn't block an added rule.

questions.question: Which change to the sharing model requires recalculating sharing for the affected records?
options: Editing a criteria-based sharing rule or bulk transferring record ownership
Adding a tab to an app
questions.explanation: Criteria rule edits and ownership transfers change the data/conditions sharing depends on, so affected records need recalculation. The other options do not affect record sharing.

questions.question: An org sets Account OWD to Private then realizes a team needs read access to all accounts. Which is the correct approach?
options: Create a criteria or ownership-based sharing rule granting that team's group read access, keeping OWD Private
questions.explanation: Keep the restrictive Private baseline and OPEN access selectively with a sharing rule to the group - the correct additive model. Relaxing OWD affects everyone and Modify All over-grants.

questions.question: A VP must view all Cases owned by reps two levels below them. Which mechanism grants this with least effort?
options: A sharing rule for each rep
Enabling 'Grant Access Using Hierarchies' for Case and placing the VP above those reps
questions.explanation: The role hierarchy (when enabled for Case) gives users implicit access to records owned below them in the chain, so the VP sees the reps' cases. Sharing rules per rep would be manual, and territories are for grouped account access.

questions.question: Which statement about the role hierarchy is TRUE?
options: It grants users access to records owned by roles above them
It grants users access to records owned by roles below them when enabled for the object
It adds sharing rows for the record owner
questions.explanation: Hierarchy access flows upward: a user sees records owned by roles beneath them. It does not reach upward or sideways, and the owner's own access is not a hierarchy share row.

questions.question: An architect wants managers to see their team's Opportunities but the Opportunity OWD is Private and the hierarchy is enabled. What else is needed?
options: Nothing - hierarchy provides manager access above the owner
questions.explanation: With Private OWD and hierarchy enabled, managers already see records owned by their subordinates via implicit hierarchy access - no additional sharing is required.

questions.question: Managers must see only the HIGH-VALUE (Amount > 100k) cases of their reps, not every case. Which mechanism is appropriate?
options: A criteria-based sharing rule targeting the managers' group
questions.explanation: Criteria-based visibility cannot be done by the hierarchy (which shares everything owned below). A criteria-based sharing rule grants only qualifying records to the managers' group.

questions.question: A hierarchy-based sharing design would generate a share row for every ancestor of every record. What is the primary risk on large data volumes?
options: Sharing table bloat and degraded performance
questions.explanation: Hierarchy-only access materializes share rows per ancestor, which on LDV inflates the sharing table and hurts performance - a core reason to prefer targeted sharing rules at scale.

questions.question: When is the role hierarchy the WRONG choice for record access?
options: When access follows the reporting line
When managers need criteria-based visibility of a subset of subordinate records
When OWD is Private and hierarchy is enabled
When records are owned by subordinates
questions.explanation: The hierarchy grants all owned records upward; it cannot restrict to criteria-based subsets. For subset visibility, use sharing rules (or restriction rules).

questions.question: An org must share all Accounts where Industry = Finance with the Finance Analysts group at Read/Write, keeping OWD Private. Which rule is correct?
options: A criteria-based sharing rule on Industry = Finance targeting the Finance Analysts group
Setting Account OWD to Public Read/Write
questions.explanation: Criteria-based sharing rules grant records matching a field condition to a target group. Ownership-based is for owner-defined sets, and relaxing OWD affects everyone.

questions.question: Which statement about sharing rules is TRUE?
options: They can share records to individual users directly
They only add access for the specified groups and cannot remove access
They apply to all users in the org
They override OWD to remove access
questions.explanation: Sharing rules are additive grants to named groups (roles, groups, territories); they cannot target a single user and cannot remove access.

questions.question: A user must access records owned by two different groups. What is the cleanest sharing-rule design?
options: Two ownership-based rules, one per source group, both granting the user's group access
One criteria rule on Owner = User
questions.explanation: Each ownership-based rule shares one source group's records to the target group; combine multiple rules to aggregate sources. Criteria rules and OWD changes do not express 'owned by specific groups' as cleanly.
